newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Fighting reported closing in on east Zaire city.
newsitem.headline: Fighting reported closing in on east Zaire city.

text.p: U.N. relief agencies and foreign embassies were seeking ways to evacuate expatriates from Kisangani on Saturday as reports of mortar fire outside the eastern city reached the Zairean capital.
"There has been fighting going on for five hours," a senior U.N. official in Kinshasa said late on Friday.
"We are looking for ways to evacuate our personnel and the French authorities are also searching for ways to help," the official said.

Aid workers in Kinshasa who were in contact with the city said the fighting began with mortar fire near the international airport on the outskirts of the town, where Zairean troops and allied foreign mercenaries are concentrated.
Diplomats reported shooting inside Kisangani itself, but it was unclear whether Zairean soldiers were fighting among themselves, looting or clashing with Tutsi-led rebels.
A defence ministry spokesman said the reports that the city was under rebel attack were false, but conceded that there may have been some shooting there.

The battle for Kisangani, the nerve centre of Zairean military operations in the east of the vast central African country, has become pivotal with both rebels and government forces concentrating troops there.

The fall of Kisangani, which the rebels claim is imminent though government forces deny this, would be the biggest setback to date for the government of ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko in a five-month rebel campaign.
Rebels who have already taken over a vaste swathe of territory in the east of Zaire have slowly surrounded the city since the beginning of the year.

Rebel leader Laurent Kabila gave Zairean generals until Thursday to lay down their weapons or face an all-out offensive on the strategic port which is situated at the head of the navigable section of the vast Zaire river.
